key_insight: Hybrid Cinematography combines physical filming with generative video reshooting so directors can preview and manage hallucination risk before leaving the set. It turns an uncertain post-production problem into an on-set decision with actionable feedback.
problem_solved: Generative reshooting can require inventing unrecorded visual content, but filmmakers often only discover these hallucinations after the shoot is over. This paper addresses the need to detect and reduce that risk early enough to still change the filming plan.
method: Uses an editable 3D shot plan to represent the intended camera move and scene composition.
Creates a proxy of the take and runs previsualization to estimate where generative reshooting would need to hallucinate missing content.
Surfaces hallucination risk during production so filmmakers can adjust the shot while they are still on set.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows how generative video systems can be paired with interactive planning tools to make outputs more reliable and controllable. It is especially relevant for human-in-the-loop workflows where safety, feasibility, and editability matter as much as generation quality.
visual_elements: A left-to-right pipeline showing physical capture, proxy take, risk estimation, and reshooting.
A 3D shot plan diagram with adjustable camera path and scene objects.
A heatmap overlay highlighting regions likely to require hallucination.
An on-set workflow icon set showing director, camera, and generative model feedback loop.
paper_title: Hybrid Cinematography: Previsualizing and Managing Hallucination Risk in Generative Video Reshooting
paper_authors: Nhan,  Tran, Neal Wadhwa, Abe Davis, Stefan Stojanov
